title: ::part() workaround & edge cases
blurb: Side-by-side migration from ::part() naming to shadowRoots, plus live failure checks for duplicate names, non-ShadowRoot/null TypeErrors, and closed shadow root encapsulation.
question: How does migrating off ::part() behave on failure boundaries such as null entries, non-ShadowRoot elements, closed roots, and cross-tree name collisions?
result: Passing null or an Element throws TypeError at dictionary conversion, closed roots cannot be opted in from outside (host.shadowRoot is null), and ::part() remains a working cross-browser fallback.
testedIn: Chrome 153 / Chromium 157 (::part() verified; shadowRoots flag inactive); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: Passing host.shadowRoot for a closed component throws TypeError because sequence<ShadowRoot> rejects null
friction.repro: Click 'shadowRoots: [closedHost.shadowRoot]' on a closed shadow host; WebIDL dictionary conversion throws TypeError before the transition starts.
friction.workaround: Filter nullable roots with .filter((r) => r instanceof ShadowRoot) before passing shadowRoots, or have the component start its own transition using its private #root reference.
